slides.title: Tuning / [chunk] size
slides.hook: Top-3 retrieval made 500-character chunks look best: 19 of 20 answers found. At a 400-character context budget, they found 9, the fewest of six sizes.
inside: A 60-character split that loses the subject
A 500-character chunk that ranks the wrong section
One context cap for every size

slides.title: One chunk, / one [vector]
slides.text: Chunk size decides what a single vector has to stand for. Test set: 6 made-up help-centre sections, 2,782 characters, 20 questions.

options.note: Sharp, but often missing its subject

slides.after: The embedding here is spaCy's `en_core_web_md`: a chunk's vector is the average of its word vectors.

slides.title: Small chunks / lose the [subject]
slides.text: At `chunk_size=60`, the audit-log answer is cut in two:

visuals.caption: chunk_size=60, chunk_overlap=0
chunks: Audit logs are kept for 1 year on the Business plan and !!3!!

bullets: "How long are audit logs kept on Enterprise?" returns "years on Enterprise." first: no number, no audit logs.

slides.title: Big chunks / [blur] facts
slides.text: Same question, two sizes: "Can I get a refund on a monthly plan?"

options.output: "Monthly plans are never refunded, but you can cancel at any time and keep access until the period ends."

options.note: No refund rule in it. The Refunds section is 2nd, at 0.916

slides.after: At 500, each vector averages about a whole section, and the two sections score 0.002 apart.

slides.title: Overlap repeats / whole [pieces]
slides.text: `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` carries over the last whole pieces that together fit in `chunk_overlap`. Measure what it adds:

options.output: 21 chunks, 2,755 characters, with or without overlap
options.note: Every piece is a paragraph, longer than 40
"plan and 3 years on Enterprise." is now one chunk

slides.after: At 60, overlap 12 moved top-3 found from 7 to 8 of 20, for 8% more text to embed and store.

slides.title: Size in the / model's [tokens]
slides.text: `chunk_size` counts characters by default (`length_function=len`). The embedding model counts tokens:
bullets: all-MiniLM-L6-v2: input longer than 256 word pieces is truncated by default (model card).
Count with the embedding model's own tokenizer.

slides.text: Found: the answer text sits whole in a retrieved chunk. Top 3 chunks at each size, spaCy vectors:

slides.title: Cap the context / [budget]
slides.text: Same test, capped at 400 characters: whole chunks in rank order while they fit, always at least one.
slides.after: At 500, one chunk already passes the cap, so it goes alone. Compare sizes at the context budget you will send to the model.

slides.after: A small, made-up test with averaged word vectors: your best size may differ.

slides.title: The tuning / [loop]
slides.text: Chunk size is a setting you measure for your documents and your model:

steps: Write 20 or more real questions, each with the text that answers it.
Split at 4 to 6 sizes, with and without overlap.
Retrieve at the context budget you will send to the model.
Count answers found whole; pick the smallest size near the top.
Re-run when documents, model or budget change.

cards.title: Sweep it when
items: Retrieved chunks come back cut mid-fact
You switch the embedding model or retriever
You change top-k or the context budget

cards.title: Move on when
items: Scores sit flat across sizes: keep the cheapest
Answers need a whole section: small-to-big retrieval
Documents have structure: split by type first

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Build 20+ questions, each with its answer text
Compare sizes at one context budget
At a fixed top-k, bigger chunks carry more text into the count
Size chunks in the embedding model's tokens
Check how many characters overlap adds
Pick the smallest size near the top score

slides.line: Chunk size decides what one vector holds. Next: what that vector is, and why texts with close meanings land close together.
